process_nodes.label: Panel-level packaging

summary: A planned chiplet and panel-level advanced packaging and test plant in Novara, Piedmont, modelled on Silicon Box's Singapore factory. The company announced the Italian project in March 2024 and chose Novara in June 2024; in December 2024 the European Commission cleared about EUR 1.3 billion of Italian aid towards a EUR 3.2 billion investment, and a development agreement with the industry ministry and Invitalia followed in March 2026. Building work, first planned for the second half of 2025, had not begun by September 2026: detailed design was under way, a building permit was still to be requested, and the mayor expected work to start by the end of spring 2027. First production had been targeted for early 2028.

location.note: A September 2026 report places the plant at Agognate, a hamlet on the edge of Novara.

metrics.note: The March and June 2024 company releases gave the investment as up to EUR 3.2 billion, together with the company's own figure of up to USD 3.6 billion; later sources drop the up-to wording (next figure).
From the December 2024 state aid decision on, the Commission, the company and September 2026 reporting give EUR 3.2 billion as the total investment, without the earlier up-to wording.
Amount given by the Piedmont regional government when the development agreement was signed; company releases and later reports still cite EUR 3.2 billion.

Direct grant under an Italian measure cleared by the European Commission in December 2024 (case SA.113264). In September 2026 Invitalia had finished its review but its board decision on the aid was still awaited.
Direct jobs at the plant at full operation, excluding construction and supplier jobs.

milestones.note: Announced a new assembly and test plant in northern Italy, subject to Commission approval of state support.
Novara chosen from a shortlist of northern Italian sites; letter of intent signed in Rome.
Original target; it passed without a reported start.
Initial production target given after the state aid approval; the site announcement said production in 2028.
In September 2026 the mayor expected work to begin by the end of the following spring, after the detailed design and building permit.

notes: Planned output at full capacity is about 10,000 panels per week, expected in 2033 (not recorded as a capacity figure because the unit is panels per week). The company says the project was granted Open EU Foundry status in March 2026. The 2025 construction target was missed and is kept as a planned milestone alongside the 2027 target.

review.method: Independent AI-assisted review (Claude): re-opened every cited source, checked each statement against it and searched for newer reporting.
review.changes: Added the March 2026 development agreement (with a EUR 3.4 billion figure from the regional government) and September 2026 reporting that construction had not started and was expected by spring 2027; changed the EUR 1.3 billion aid from awarded to committed because the national grant decision was still pending, added Invitalia and the Agognate location, and refreshed the status date. Audit fixes (2026-11-07): kept the up-to and exact EUR 3.2 billion figures as different statements from different dates and explained the change in their notes; confirmed that the USD 3.6 billion in the note is the company's own figure, not a conversion.
